title: Senior's toolkit: tests in the pipeline
summary: dotnet test with filters, reports, hang dumps and coverage, plus service containers, test artifacts and hunting a flaky test.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: tests in the pipeline
steps.body: A test job should run the right tests, leave a report behind even when it fails, and never hang. These flags and keys do that (shown for `dotnet test` in its default VSTest mode).

toolkit.what: Runs a subset of tests: fast unit tests on every push, slow integration tests in their own job.
flags: skip tests with that trait or category
combine conditions with or and and

toolkit.what: Tests the exact binaries the build step produced instead of compiling again.
flags: fail if it was not built, instead of building silently
toolkit.example: dotnet build -c Release && dotnet test -c Release --no-build

toolkit.what: Writes machine-readable results that CI test reporters and PR annotations read.
flags: a TRX file with a fixed name

toolkit.what: If a test hangs longer than this, collect a dump and fail, instead of waiting for the job timeout. Names the test that hung.
flags: collect a dump when the test host crashes

toolkit.what: Collects line and branch coverage with coverlet (the `coverlet.collector` package, in the default xUnit template). `reportgenerator` turns it into HTML or a summary.
Uploads the test results even when the test step failed, which is exactly when you need them.
flags: run after success or failure, not after a cancel
toolkit.example:
- uses: actions/upload-artifact@v5
  if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
  with:
    name: test-results
    path: TestResults

toolkit.what: Runs a real dependency (Postgres, Redis) as a container next to the job, so integration tests hit the real thing.
flags: reach it on localhost from the job
wait until it is healthy before the steps run
toolkit.example:
services:
  db:
    image: postgres:17
    env:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: test
    ports: ['5432:5432']
    options: >-
      --health-cmd "pg_isready -U postgres" --health-interval 5s --health-retries 10

toolkit.cmd: for i in $(seq 30); do dotnet test --no-build --filter <test> || break; done
toolkit.what: Runs one suspect test many times to prove it is flaky (and to prove your fix). One pass proves nothing.
flags: stop at the first failure and keep its output
toolkit.example: for i in $(seq 30); do dotnet test --no-build --filter "FullyQualifiedName~CheckoutTests.Applies_discount" || break; done

steps.prompt: The test job failed, and the "Upload test results" step after it shows as skipped, so there is no report to read. What do you change?
options: Add `continue-on-error: true` to the test step
Move the upload to a separate workflow
steps.explain: Steps run only after success by default. A status condition makes the upload run after a failure too. `continue-on-error` would turn the red test job green, which hides the failure.

steps.prompt: Match the flag to its meaning.
pairs: test the binaries the build step already made
dump and fail a test that hangs
write results a CI reporter can read
record which lines the tests ran

steps.prompt: Run the unit tests on the Release build without compiling again, and keep a results file.
steps.explain: `--no-build` reuses the build output, `--filter` picks the tests, `--logger trx` writes the results file.

steps.prompt: `CheckoutTests.Applies_discount` fails about once in fifteen CI runs and always passes on your laptop. What is the right next step?
options: Run it in a loop (`--filter` plus a `for` loop) until it fails, then read that failure; look for shared state, time or ordering
Add a retry so the job passes
steps.explain: You fix a flaky test by reproducing it. A loop turns one-in-fifteen into a failure within minutes. Retries can buy time while you fix it, but a test that sometimes fails is telling you about a real race or a hidden dependency.

steps.prompt: Unit test job or integration test job?
items: Runs on every push in under two minutes
Needs a health check before the tests start

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: Build once and test with `--no-build`, always upload results with a status condition, and give test runs a hang timeout. When a test flakes, loop it until it fails instead of re-running the pipeline.
